scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The drama serves as social satire, mocking the landed gentry and exploring the domestic problems of wives.
Unlike other mask dances, it lacks exorcism ceremonies, functioning primarily as a form of communal entertainment and social critique.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is characterized by the Youngnam province style, featuring specific lines, masks, and costumes that have remained close to their original forms.
It consists of five stories or acts.
The movement is described as natural and fluid, often performed by men who are also farmers, blending agricultural rhythms with dramatic storytelling.
Watch for Youngnam Style.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performers wear traditional masks and costumes specific to the Youngnam style.
Historically performed on the 15th day of the New Year (lunar calendar), it is now typically staged in Spring and Autumn in Goseong, Gyeongsangnam-do.
on_screen: Images — MISSING
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Yi Yunseok is the current National Human Treasure (보유자) and is famously known as the 'dancing farmer.' Other key performers include An Daecheon, Choe Yeongho, Heo Changyeol, and Seon Yeong-uk, who have expanded the dance's reach through modern troupes.
Goseong ogwangdae is noted for having the most 'Youngnam province style' compared to other regional versions like Tongyeong Ogwangdae, due to its preservation of original lines and mask designs.

The tradition is preserved by the Goseong Ogwangdae Preservation Association and has influenced modern performing groups like 'The Gwangdae' and 'Cheonha Jeiltal,' which perform mask dance dramas nationally.
